To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the entropy generation decreases by increasing the inclination angle of magnetic field.
the total and local entropy generation decrease when the magnetic field is applied to the enclosure.
the magnetic field reduces the heat transfer and fluid circulation in the enclosure and that the entropy generation decreases with increasing the inclination angle of magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the magnetic field inclination angle on the entropy generation in a square cavity filled with air or liquid gallium, in a steady-unsteady state.
the entropy generation in natural convective flows of air and liquid gallum in the presence of an externally applied magnetic field.
the entropy generation and the heat transfer in natural convection with an external magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the total irreversibility decreases with increasing Hartmann number, while it increases with increasing Grashof number.
the total entropy generation in the enclosure is decreased by the magnetic field and the inclination angle of it.
the entropy generation in natural-convection is reduced when an external oriented magnetic filed is imposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic field has a significant effect on the total irreversibility, the heat transfer, the fluid flow and the local irreversibility.
the magnetic field has the same effects on entropy generation and heat transfer.
the total irreversibility is increased with increasing the Prandtl and the Grashof numbers, but decreased with increasing Hartmann, the irreversibilities coefficients, and the inclination angles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropy generation is a function of the magnetic field strength, the inclination angle, the thermal Grushof number, and the Prandtl Number.
the entropy generation in natural convective flows can be minimized by applying an external magnetic field with a suitable inclination angle.
